content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation on § 14.2 (critical, ip-data).**

**What I found across the document:**
- **§ 14.2 (p0054)** — the problem: Vendor "exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer," and we get only a **revocable, non-transferable** licence lasting only the Order Form term. Under the definition in § 1.4, Deliverables are bespoke reports, configurations, integrations, designs, workflows and training material created specifically for us — i.e. exactly what we pay for.
- **§ 13.2 (p0049)** — the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence exists, but only for "software and Vendor Technology delivered … on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable" — it does not license the Deliverable itself, so it does not rescue § 14.2. There is no sublicence right anywhere in the document.
- **§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 15.1, 1.8** — already at our preferred position: we own Customer Data and our independent IP with no transfer to Vendor; Vendor retains Vendor Technology (defined as its pre-existing tools) and routes embedded Vendor IP to the § 13.2 perpetual licence; no joint IP absent a signed instrument identifying exploitation rights.

Because the fallback licence elements (perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free, modify, sublicense) are all absent for Deliverables and the surrounding architecture is otherwise at preferred, the shortest complete fix was to flip § 14.2 only:

> "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable **and other work product** created for Customer, **and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable and work product.**"

Vendor's platform, generic tools and know-how are untouched (expressly excluded from Deliverables by §§ 1.4 and 1.8), and the fallback licence structure is offered in the comment if Vendor must retain title. Redline validated (ok:true, minimality passed) before submission.
